question: What is the primary goal of diagnostic investigations in the intensive care unit?

options.A: Identifying rapid physiological changes before organ failure
options.B: Complying with mandatory annual accreditation rules
options.C: Reducing the overall cost of hospital admission
options.D: Providing material for medical student lectures

explanation: Critical care diagnostics aim to detect sudden physiological shifts early to prevent organ damage. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h1)

question: How do critical care diagnostics differ from tests performed on a standard general ward?

options.A: They are performed continuously and simultaneously
options.B: They take days to yield any usable clinical results
options.C: They only involve blood samples and never imaging
options.D: They are ordered exclusively by senior consultants

explanation: Intensive care requires constant, simultaneous monitoring to keep pace with unstable patient conditions. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which anatomical landmark aligns with the transducer during arterial line zeroing?
explanation: The transducer must align with the phlebostatic axis, which corresponds to the right atrium, to ensure accurate pressure readings. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is the Allen test performed prior to radial artery cannulation?

options.A: To determine the correct size of the catheter sheath
options.B: To check for systemic blood clotting abnormalities
options.C: To evaluate collateral ulnar circulation to the hand
options.D: To measure baseline systolic blood pressure accurately

explanation: The Allen test ensures the ulnar artery can supply blood to the hand if the radial artery becomes occluded by the catheter. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the normal reference range for blood pH in an adult?
explanation: A normal physiological pH falls strictly between 7.35 and 7.45, with values outside this range indicating acidosis or alkalosis. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h3)

question: An arterial blood gas report shows an elevated PaCO2 and a decreased pH. What condition does this indicate?
explanation: High carbon dioxide levels act as an acid in the body, lowering the pH and causing respiratory acidosis. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h3)

question: Elevated serum lactate levels in a critically ill patient most directly indicate what condition?
explanation: Lactate is a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, which increases when cells do not receive enough oxygen during shock or low perfusion states. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why are serial laboratory draws preferred over single, isolated test results in intensive care?

options.A: Serial draws prevent the development of anemia
options.B: Laboratories cannot process single specimens accurately
options.C: Single values are prohibited by hospital protocol
options.D: Trends reveal whether current treatments are effective

explanation: Looking at how lab values change over time helps the clinical team see if the patient is improving or deteriorating under treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of point-of-care ultrasound for unstable intensive care patients?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for mechanical ventilation
options.B: It eliminates the need to transport the patient out of the unit
options.C: It measures intracranial pressure without invasive hardware
options.D: It provides permanent laboratory blood chemistry results

explanation: Bringing the ultrasound machine to the bedside keeps unstable patients safe by avoiding risky journeys to radiology departments. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which clinical procedure is commonly guided by point-of-care ultrasound to improve patient safety?
explanation: Ultrasound guidance helps clinicians visualize blood vessels directly, reducing complications like accidental arterial puncture during line placement. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h5)

question: What device is used to monitor brain tissue swelling and pressure directly in severe head injuries?
explanation: An intracranial pressure monitor is surgically placed to track brain tissue pressure and prevent dangerous secondary brain injury. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary nursing priority when preparing an unstable patient for a computed tomography scan outside the unit?

options.A: Maintaining continuous monitoring and life support stability
options.B: Removing all intravenous lines to speed up the scan
options.C: Ensuring the patient has eaten a full meal beforehand
options.D: Discontinuing all mechanical ventilation support temporarily

explanation: Transporting critically ill patients carries risks, so nurses must ensure portable life support and monitoring remain uninterrupted. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility before any diagnostic procedure in the intensive care unit?

options.A: Writing the official diagnostic radiology report
options.B: Ordering replacement lab reagents from the pharmacy
options.C: Verifying the patient's identity and procedure consent
options.D: Calibrating the main hospital electrical power grid

explanation: Ensuring correct patient identification and valid consent prevents procedural errors and protects patient rights. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must nurses monitor equipment alarms closely during diagnostic testing?

options.A: To ensure the battery chargers are plugged into the wall
options.B: To detect sudden physiological deterioration or technical dislodgement
options.C: To prevent the monitoring screens from dimming over time
options.D: To comply with noise level regulations set by the hospital

explanation: Alarms give early warnings of dangerous changes in patient status or equipment failures like a dislodged arterial line. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h7)
